_comment: The Sourdough Dynasty — a genealogy of one starter and the fates of its heirs.
Two properties, one of which is a negative result worth keeping.
First, diamonds: flows split and rejoin on the same downstream node — both
feeding regimes reach 'an actual loaf', and three of the four generations reach
'hooch'. No other fixture has split-and-rejoin at this density, and it is what
makes link stacking order (by the vertical centre of the band at the far end)
observable on a small graph.
Second, and this is the deliberate part: 'gifted onward' splits 3,300 / 3,300
between religious and occasional feeding, so two sibling links carry *equal*
flow. It is tempting to assume that makes the diagram sensitive to input order,
since input order is the last of the four tie-breaks (subtree size, then
degree, then flow descending, then input order). It does not: reversing this
dataset's link list produces identical geometry, because subtree size and
degree separate the two candidates long before flow is compared.
So this fixture is the standing counter-example to 'equal flows make order
matter'. The dataset that *is* order-sensitive is catday, which has no equal
sibling flows at all — see its `orderSensitive` note. Keeping both pinned is
what documents that the chain is a sequence of stable sorts rather than one
combined key.
A forgotten starter at 5g gives the thin node for the label drop rule.
Flows are grams of flour and conserve to 64,000 exactly.
Regenerate the derived files with: node tools/generate_golden.mjs
title: The Sourdough Dynasty
blurb: Diamonds that split and rejoin, plus equal sibling flows that the earlier tie-breaks resolve anyway.
